notes: Rechecked after ip#220, which changed the proof-setup and latch sentences to match the gate. The earlier record (2026-11-13) named the previous bytes and is replaced.

Reset every flop: lowRISC says sequential statements for state assignments should contain only reset values and the next-state assignment, and its resets are active-low and asynchronous by default; the document's rule that every flop holding state gets a reset value is read from that line. lowRISC does not itself say every flop must be reset.

Verilator: always @(x) is recomputed on a possible change of its inputs as Design Compiler would synthesize it, where a compliant simulator recomputes only when x changes; full_case, parallel_case, unique and priority are proven or asserted at run time unless --no-assert-case is given (the document does not mention the option, which is fine). The two-state notes and the zeros, ones, random reset check are in the Unknown States section.

SBY: depth defaults to 20 for bmc and cover and is the k-induction depth for the smtbmc engine in prove mode; a cover run fails if a cover cannot be reached within depth or only by breaking an assertion; always @(*) and clocked assertions differ by one step; (* anyconst *) is the solver-chosen constant used for memories. The reference page lists [tasks], [options], [engines], [script] and [files]; that [engines] and [script] are required by the gate is not claimed by the gate code (see gate_claims).
ZipCPU: the f_past_valid register and the assumption that reset is active on the first cycle are in the section Capturing the rules in formal properties.

Checked against the gate: the cover run reuses the proof's [options] lines except mode, so the proof's depth is also the cover's depth (eda.py:726-731). The document says a cover fails if it cannot be reached within the depth, which is correct for the gate, and it makes no claim that a short depth suffices.

gate_claims.claim: the lint, simulation, synthesis and formal tools are run by the platform and the seat has none
the platform runs lint, simulation, synthesis, formal and cover as brokered backends
the platform's synthesis script is fixed (read_verilog, synth -top, stat), so the seat cannot pass -latches error
any latch fails the gate: synthesis counts latch cells and the rtl stage bounds them at 0
any latch fails the gate: the bound on latches is at most 0 on the rtl stage
the card's procedures fix the verdict line and who may call $finish
the verdict line is NIRMAAN-SIM nonce passed, failed, printed once before $finish
only the testbench may call $finish, $stop or read plusargs; a design that does is refused
Verilator simulation is built with --binary so $value$plusargs works
submit one .sby with no [tasks]; a setup with [tasks] is refused and nothing runs
the formal check refuses a [tasks] setup before running
the cover check also refuses a [tasks] setup
[options] needs mode prove; bmc is a bounded check and fails (proven is 0 in bmc mode)
[options] needs mode prove; the requirement carries the bound proven at least 1
[files] must list every RTL file submitted, by path from the .sby's directory
sby runs in the .sby file's own directory, so [files] paths resolve there
depth defaults to 20 when [options] names none
the platform runs the cover separately in cover mode, rewriting only mode and the file paths
the cover run needs an [options] section to rewrite
write at least one cover: a run that reaches no cover fails
every cover must be reachable: an unreached cover fails the run as vacuous
every assertion's antecedent must be reachable: an unreached antecedent fails the run
the cover check is required when a .sby is produced
[engines] and [script] (read the sources, then prep -top) are part of the setup
depth is the induction depth in prove mode, per the SBY reference
